text: Based on the evidence, yes, the property did lose tree cover in 2019. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) observed a tree-cover loss event of 1.8 hectares on the property in that year. This loss was corroborated by the JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 dataset, which mapped the entire event area as forest in 2020, suggesting that the area was indeed forested prior to the loss. Additionally, the Uruguay Ministry of Livestock, Agriculture and Fisheries (MGAP) forest map confirmed that the area affected was planted forest, specifically with Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda species.
